FSSPEC_ABI_VERSION is the version the header describes; fsspec_abi_version() returns the version the loaded library was built with. Both are 1. Every vtable and factory struct starts with struct_size and abi_version. Registration fails with FSSPEC_INVALID_ARGUMENT when abi_version differs from the library’s, or when struct_size is smaller than those two fields or larger than 64 KiB. A struct shorter than the library’s is accepted; the missing trailing fields are treated as null.

Every fallible function returns fsspec_status, an int32_t: Code Value Rust FsError FSSPEC_OK 0 FSSPEC_NOT_FOUND 1 NotFound FSSPEC_PERMISSION_DENIED 2 PermissionDenied FSSPEC_ALREADY_EXISTS 3 AlreadyExists FSSPEC_NOT_A_DIRECTORY 4 NotADirectory FSSPEC_IS_A_DIRECTORY 5 IsADirectory FSSPEC_IO 6 IoError FSSPEC_INVALID_ARGUMENT 7 InvalidArgument FSSPEC_NOT_SUPPORTED 8 NotSupported FSSPEC_OTHER 9 Other Function Description fsspec_last_error_message() Message for the last failure on the calling thread, or null. Valid until the next failure on that thread. fsspec_set_last_error(message, len) Sets the thread’s message. Foreign backends call it before returning a failing status. fsspec_clear_last_error() Clears the thread’s message. Panics inside libfsspec are caught at the boundary and returned as FSSPEC_OTHER.

Arguments are UTF-8 pointer and length pairs and need no NUL terminator. Values that libfsspec returns are owned by the caller and freed with the matching function: Type Fields Free with fsspec_string data (NUL-terminated), len (without the NUL) fsspec_string_free fsspec_string_list items, len fsspec_string_list_free fsspec_bytes data, len fsspec_bytes_free fsspec_file_info name, size, file_type, created_ns, modified_ns, extra fsspec_file_info_free fsspec_file_info_list items, len fsspec_file_info_list_free created_ns and modified_ns are nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, or -1 when unknown. file_type is FSSPEC_FILE_TYPE_FILE, FSSPEC_FILE_TYPE_DIRECTORY, or FSSPEC_FILE_TYPE_OTHER. extra contains backend-specific fields as alternating key and value strings. All of these buffers use the platform allocator: malloc on Unix and HeapAlloc(GetProcessHeap(), ...) on Windows. Foreign backends allocate the values they return through vtable callbacks the same way, and libfsspec frees them.

fsspec_options is a string-to-string map. Function Description fsspec_options_new() Creates an empty map. fsspec_options_set(options, key, key_len, value, value_len) Sets a key, replacing an earlier value. fsspec_options_items(options, out) Alternating key and value strings, sorted by key. fsspec_options_free(options) Frees the map. Null is ignored. A null fsspec_options * argument means no options.

Function Description fsspec_url_to_fs(url, url_len, options, out_fs, out_path) Resolves a URL through the registry. out_path, when not null, receives the path to use with the filesystem. fsspec_register_filesystem(protocol, protocol_len, factory) Registers a factory, replacing an earlier one and dropping its cached instances. The factory struct is copied. fsspec_protocols(out) Registered protocols, sorted. fsspec_register_fallback(factory) Installs the factory used for protocols nothing registered; null clears it. It is given the whole URL. URL resolution, caching, and the built-in protocols (file, local, memory, s3) and their options are the same as the Rust registry; see “Filesystem registry” in the Rust reference. fsspec_fs_factory: Field Description struct_size sizeof(fsspec_fs_factory) abi_version FSSPEC_ABI_VERSION data Passed to every callback. create Required. Builds a filesystem for a path and options; returns it in out. instance_scope Optional. Returns the part of the path that needs its own instance, such as a bucket. release Optional. Called with data when the registry drops the factory, such as when it is replaced.

With detail false, entries may contain only names. fsspec_fs_info(fs, path, path_len, out) Metadata for one path. fsspec_fs_exists(fs, path, path_len, out) Whether a path exists. fsspec_fs_cat_file(fs, path, path_len, start, end, out) Reads a file, or [*start, *end) when the pointers are not null. fsspec_file * is an open file, closed with fsspec_file_close. Function Description fsspec_file_read(file, buf, len, out_read) Reads up to len bytes; *out_read is zero at end of file. fsspec_file_write(file, data, len, out_written) Writes bytes; out_written may be null. fsspec_file_seek(file, offset, whence, out_position) whence is 0 (start), 1 (current), or 2 (end). fsspec_file_tell(file, out_position) Current offset. fsspec_file_flush(file) Flushes buffered writes. fsspec_file_size(file, out_size) Size, or -1 when unknown. fsspec_file_get_info(file, out) Metadata for the open file. fsspec_file_commit(file), fsspec_file_discard(file) Commits or discards a transactional write. fsspec_file_close(file) Flushes and frees the handle. The handle is freed even when the flush fails. Null is ignored.

fsspec_fs_from_vtable(vtable, data) wraps an implementation written outside libfsspec as an fsspec_fs *, and fsspec_file_from_vtable(vtable, data) does the same for an open file. Both copy the vtable, pass data to every callback, and return null with the error message set on failure. fsspec_fs_vtable: Field Description struct_size, abi_version As for factories. protocol NUL-terminated, comma-separated protocol names, such as "file,local". root_marker, sep NUL-terminated strings; null uses the defaults. ls, info, rm_file, cp_file, mkdir, rmdir, open The FileSystem primitives. A null callback makes its operation return FSSPEC_NOT_SUPPORTED. Other operations, such as cat_file and exists, are derived from these. release Called with data when the last handle is released. strip_protocol, unstrip_protocol, cat_file, pipe_file Optional, after release. A backend that overrides these in Rust keeps its own behaviour across the ABI; null uses the derived defaults. fsspec_file_vtable has read, write, seek, flush, size, info, commit, discard, and release. A null read, write, seek, or info returns FSSPEC_NOT_SUPPORTED; a null size reports -1; a null flush, commit, or discard succeeds without doin

The fsspec_sys crate declares the C functions without a #[link] attribute; the build links libfsspec (hatch-rs links) or compiles fsspec_capi in. It contains no registry state. t: Why fsspec-rs uses explicit protocols and shared traits
x: Why fsspec-rs uses explicit protocols and shared traits fsspec-rs provides Python’s fsspec interface and a Rust filesystem trait. Python applications can select a Rust-backed filesystem through fsspec, while Rust applications can use the native backends without Python. A separate bridge crate lets Rust callers use Python fsspec implementations through the same trait. Explicit protocols preserve compatibility fsspec already assigns file, local, memory, and s3 to established Python implementations. Replacing those registrations globally would make importing fsspec-rs change unrelated application behavior. The file-rs, local-rs, memory-rs, and s3-rs names make backend selection explicit in configuration and allow both implementations to coexist. The classes still inherit from fsspec.spec.AbstractFileSystem. Code written against fsspec operations can therefore select a Rust backend without switching to a different API. Default methods keep native backends small The Rust FileSystem trait follows fsspec’s template-method pattern. x: fsspec already assigns file, local, memory, and s3 to established Python implementations. Replacing those registrations globally would make importing fsspec-rs change unrelated application behavior. The file-rs, local-rs, memory-rs, and s3-rs names make backend selection explicit in configuration and allow both implementations to coexist. The classes still inherit from fsspec.spec.AbstractFileSystem. Code written against fsspec operations can therefore select a Rust backend without switching to a different API.

t: Why fsspec-rs uses explicit protocols and shared traits
s: Default methods keep native backends small
x: The Rust FileSystem trait follows fsspec’s template-method pattern. A backend implements primitive operations such as listing files, reading metadata, opening files, copying, and removing files. Default trait methods build higher-level operations such as walking, recursive removal, and local transfers from those primitives. This design centralizes shared path and traversal behavior while leaving storage-specific I/O in LocalFs and S3Fs. Default methods may miss backend-specific optimizations, so backends can override them where needed.

t: Why fsspec-rs uses explicit protocols and shared traits
s: The Python bridge is a separate crate
x: The fsspec_rs_bridge crate adapts an installed Python filesystem to the Rust trait, so a Rust component running inside Python can use protocols that have no native Rust implementation. The bridge depends on PyO3 and a Python runtime, while the core fsspec_rs crate does not. Keeping them in separate crates lets standalone Rust applications avoid the Python dependency. Native backends avoid calls into Python; the bridge provides access to Python backends when no native implementation is available.

t: Why fsspec-rs uses explicit protocols and shared traits
x: The local and S3 backends implement the synchronous FileSystem trait. S3 runs async object-store calls through an internal Tokio runtime. Callers use a synchronous interface that matches Python file objects and fsspec, but cannot control async scheduling. The experimental AsyncFileSystem trait defines an async interface without changing the synchronous one. Its status and methods are documented in the Rust reference.

t: Why fsspec-rs uses explicit protocols and shared traits
x: A Rust crate compiled into a Python extension is private to that extension. When fsspec-rs, fsspec-db, and fsspec-kafka each compile fsspec_rs in, a process loads three copies of its code and three registries, so a backend registered by one extension is invisible to the others. Rust has no stable ABI, so a dyn FileSystem cannot be passed from one extension to another either. libfsspec fixes both with a C ABI. The registry, its instance cache, and the built-in backends are compiled into that one shared library, and every extension links it dynamically. A filesystem is passed between extensions as an opaque handle with a table of C function pointers, which every compiler and language supports. The work is split across three crates so that only one of them has shared state: fsspec_rs has the traits and backends. Compiling the traits into several extensions is harmless; its own registry stays private to the binary that compiles it in. fsspec_capi builds libfsspec and is the only crate with the shared registry. fsspec_sys declares the C functions without implementing them. Extensions depend on it to reach libfsspec; it must never depend on fsspec_capi, or every extension would export it

fsspec-rs filesystems fsspec-rs provides Rust-backed filesystems through fsspec classes. Importing fsspec_rs registers the protocols with fsspec: Filesystem Protocols Class Local filesystem file-rs, local-rs fsspec_rs.LocalFileSystem In memory memory-rs fsspec_rs.MemoryFileSystem Amazon S3 s3-rs fsspec_rs.S3FileSystem The standard file, local, memory, and s3 registrations remain unchanged. import fsspec import fsspec_rs with fsspec.open("file-rs:///tmp/example.txt", "rb") as f: data = f.read() Local filesystem LocalFileSystem wraps the Rust LocalFs backend, which uses std::fs for local paths. It is marked as a local filesystem (local_file = True) and implements fsspec’s core filesystem operations. from fsspec_rs import LocalFileSystem fs = LocalFileSystem(auto_mkdir=True) fs.pipe_file("/tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt", b"hello") assert fs.exists("/tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt") assert fs.isfile("/tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt") print(fs.info("/tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt")) Local paths Direct method calls use normal local paths: fs.cat_file("/tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt") fsspec URLs use file-rs:// or local-rs://: with fsspec.open("local-rs:///tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt", "rb") as f: print(f.read()

LocalFileSystem wraps the Rust LocalFs backend, which uses std::fs for local paths. It is marked as a local filesystem (local_file = True) and implements fsspec’s core filesystem operations. from fsspec_rs import LocalFileSystem fs = LocalFileSystem(auto_mkdir=True) fs.pipe_file("/tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt", b"hello") assert fs.exists("/tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt") assert fs.isfile("/tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt") print(fs.info("/tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt"))

Direct method calls use normal local paths: fs.cat_file("/tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt") fsspec URLs use file-rs:// or local-rs://: with fsspec.open("local-rs:///tmp/fsspec-rs/example.txt", "rb") as f: print(f.read()) LocalFileSystem._strip_protocol() removes only the Rust-specific local protocols. The file:// and local:// protocols still select fsspec’s Python implementation.

Supported modes are rb, wb, ab, and xb, plus the aliases r, w, a, and x at the Rust layer. Python wrappers expose binary file objects that implement read, write, seek, tell, flush, close, readable, writable, and seekable. with fs.open("/tmp/fsspec-rs/out.bin", "wb") as f: f.write(b"payload") with fs.open("/tmp/fsspec-rs/out.bin", "rb") as f: f.seek(2) print(f.read()) auto_mkdir=True creates missing parent directories for write, append, exclusive-create, and copy operations. With the default auto_mkdir=False, the operating system reports an error if a parent directory is missing. wb and xb files are buffered in memory and written when the file is closed. The contents go to a temporary file next to the target, which is synced and then renamed over the target, so other readers see either the previous contents or the complete new contents. flush() does not make partial contents visible. xb fails at close if another writer created the file after it was opened. ab files append to the target directly.

Local filesystem methods delegated to Rust include: Listing and metadata: ls, info, exists, isdir, isfile, size Reads and writes: open, cat_file, pipe_file, head, tail, read_text, write_text, touch Directory operations: mkdir, makedirs, rmdir, walk, find, du Mutation and transfer: rm_file, rm, cp_file, copy, mv, get_file, put_file The cache_type, block_size, and max_blocks options are accepted by open() for API compatibility but do not change local read behavior. Local reads use direct filesystem operations.

MemoryFileSystem wraps the Rust MemoryFs backend, which keeps files in process memory. Every instance shares one store, so a file written through one MemoryFileSystem is visible through all of them until the process exits. import fsspec from fsspec_rs import MemoryFileSystem fs = MemoryFileSystem() fs.pipe_file("/data/example.txt", b"hello") with fsspec.open("memory-rs://data/example.txt", "rb") as f: print(f.read()) Paths are rooted at /. Writing a file needs no mkdir: directories exist while a file below them does, as in fsspec’s MemoryFileSystem. mkdir creates an empty directory that persists until rmdir or rm. Written files become visible when they are closed, so readers never see partial contents. The store is separate from fsspec’s Python memory://. In Rust, and to C, C++, and other extensions through libfsspec, the same store is memory://.

S3FileSystem wraps the Rust S3Fs backend, which uses Apache Arrow’s object_store crate and runs its async S3 calls through an embedded Tokio runtime. The Python protocol is s3-rs, so it can coexist with s3fs. from fsspec_rs import S3FileSystem fs = S3FileSystem(bucket="my-bucket", region="us-east-1") fs.pipe_file("reports/hello.txt", b"hello") print(fs.cat_file("reports/hello.txt"))

S3FileSystem is constructed for one bucket. Method calls can use keys within that bucket: fs.ls("reports") fs.info("reports/hello.txt") fsspec URLs include the bucket. _get_kwargs_from_urls() extracts constructor options from the URL: with fsspec.open( "s3-rs://my-bucket/reports/hello.txt", "rb", region="us-east-1", ) as f: print(f.read()) Object names are stored internally without a leading slash. Directory entries are S3 prefixes, not real directories; mkdir() and rmdir() are no-ops.

Credential resolution follows this order: Explicit constructor arguments: key, secret, token, region, endpoint_url, and anon fsspec.config.conf["s3"], including values populated from fsspec config environment variables object_store’s own AWS credential chain, such as environment variables, profiles, and instance or task roles client_kwargs={"endpoint_url": ...} is accepted for compatibility with s3fs. The Rust backend allows plain HTTP when the endpoint starts with http://, as used by local S3-compatible services. fs = S3FileSystem( bucket="benchmark", key="minioadmin", secret="minioadmin", endpoint_url="http://localhost:9000", region="us-east-1", ) Anonymous access is available with anon=True.

S3 reads support optional Rust-side cache strategies through cache_type: cache_type Behavior none Fetch each requested byte range directly. readahead Keep one lookahead window for sequential reads. block Cache fixed-size blocks with LRU eviction. all Fetch the whole object on first read. with fs.open( "large/table.parquet", "rb", cache_type="block", block_size=8 * 1024 * 1024, ) as f: header = f.read(4096) block_size defaults to 4 MiB, and the Rust max_blocks default is 32. The Python file wrapper does not forward max_blocks from open(), so callers cannot change it through that method. Without an explicit cache_type, S3 read mode eagerly loads the whole object into memory. Explicit readahead, block, and none select range-based reads.

S3 methods delegated to Rust include: Listing and metadata: ls, info, exists, isdir, isfile, size Reads and writes: open, cat_file, pipe_file, head, tail, read_text Prefix traversal: walk, find Object mutation: rm_file, rm, cp_file S3 writes buffer object contents in memory before upload. The public API does not support concurrent multipart uploads or signed URLs.

s: Limit memory use for S3 reads
x: Choose an explicit cache strategy when opening large objects. Omitting cache_type eagerly reads the whole S3 object: with fs.open( "tables/orders.parquet", "rb", cache_type="block", block_size=8 * 1024 * 1024, ) as file: header = file.read(64 * 1024) The Python wrapper uses the Rust default of 32 cached blocks; it does not forward max_blocks. Choose none for direct range fetches, readahead for sequential access, or block for repeated random access. Use all only when you want to fetch the whole object on first read. See the filesystem reference for cache behavior and supported operations.

s: Check a filesystem as a records store
x: Applications that keep one file per record, such as fsspec.get_mapper stores, need atomic replacement, durable writes, complete listings, and FileNotFoundError for missing records. fsspec_rs.testing.records checks these guarantees for any fsspec URL. Import its tests into a test module and define a unique empty root and its storage options: import pytest from fsspec_rs.testing.records import * # noqa: F403 @pytest.fixture def records_url(tmp_path): return f"file-rs://{tmp_path}/records" @pytest.fixture def records_storage_options(): return {"auto_mkdir": True} Storage options must be JSON-serializable, because one test reopens the store in a separate process. file-rs, s3-rs, and s3fs pass. fsspec’s file protocol fails the replacement test because it writes directly to the target.

x: A backend registered in libfsspec can be opened by every consumer in the process, whatever language it is written in. Register it once, when your library loads. Rust Register a factory from the extension’s module initializer. Any closure from a path and options to a SharedFileSystem is a factory: use std::sync::Arc; use fsspec_rs::{FsOptions, FsResult, SharedFileSystem}; use pyo3::exceptions::PyRuntimeError; use pyo3::prelude::*; #[pymodule] fn my_extension(m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> { fsspec_sys::register_filesystem( "example", |_path: &str, options: &FsOptions| -> FsResult<SharedFileSystem> { Ok(Arc::new(ExampleFs::new(options)?)) }, ) .map_err(|error| PyRuntimeError::new_err(error.to_string()))?; Ok(()) } fsspec_sys exports ExampleFs through the vtables, so C and C++ callers see every FileSystem method it implements. s: Ship a wheel that links libfsspec
x: Wheel repair tools copy external libraries into the wheel by default, which would give your package its own copy of libfsspec and its own registry. Exclude it: auditwheel repair --exclude 'libfsspec.so*' dist/*.whl delvewheel repair --exclude fsspec.dll dist/*.whl On macOS, delocate resolves every dependency before it applies --exclude, and your extension’s @rpath only finds libfsspec inside an environment where fsspec_rs is installed. Put the library from an fsspec-rs wheel on DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH while repairing: python -m pip download --no-deps --only-binary=:all: --dest fsspec-rs-wheel 'fsspec-rs>=0.2.1,<0.3' python -m zipfile -e fsspec-rs-wheel/fsspec_rs-*.whl fsspec-rs-wheel DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=fsspec-rs-wheel/fsspec_rs/lib delocate-wheel --exclude libfsspec dist/*.whl Require fsspec-rs at run time, at least the version you built against: [project] dependencies = ["fsspec-rs>=0.2"] To fail early on a mismatched library, compare fsspec_abi_version() with FSSPEC_ABI_VERSION (fsspec_sys::abi_version() in Rust) when your library loads.

Cache and CacheType Read cache strategy interface and selector.

LocalFs and S3Fs implement the synchronous FileSystem trait. Backends must implement seven primitive methods and protocol: use fsspec_rs::{FileInfo, FileSystem, FsFile, FsResult, OpenMode, OpenOptions}; struct MyFs; impl FileSystem for MyFs { fn protocol(&self) -> &[&str] { &["myfs"] } fn ls(&self, path: &str, detail: bool) -> FsResult<Vec<FileInfo>> { todo!() } fn rm_file(&self, path: &str) -> FsResult<()> { todo!() } fn cp_file(&self, src: &str, dst: &str) -> FsResult<()> { todo!() } fn open( &self, path: &str, mode: OpenMode, opts: Option<OpenOptions>, ) -> FsResult<Box<dyn FsFile>> { todo!() } fn info(&self, path: &str) -> FsResult<FileInfo> { todo!() } fn mkdir(&self, path: &str, create_parents: bool) -> FsResult<()> { todo!() } fn rmdir(&self, path: &str) -> FsResult<()> { todo!() } } root_marker() defaults to "" and sep() defaults to "/". Backends can override them for local or platform-specific behavior. strip_protocol() and unstrip_protocol() also have defaults and can be overridden when a backend needs bucket-aware or authority-aware paths. The default methods built on those primitives include: Path helpers: strip_protocol, unstrip_protocol, parent Metadata checks: exists

AsyncFileSystem is the experimental async version of FileSystem. Its primitive methods return futures, and its default helpers are async fns. LocalFs and S3Fs implement only the synchronous FileSystem trait. The default async implementation avoids recursive async futures in walk() by using an explicit stack. Method semantics otherwise match FileSystem.

FileSystem::open() returns a file implementing FsFile, which requires Read + Write + Seek + Send. commit() and discard() default to no-ops and are available for buffered writes or future transaction support.

FileInfo is the common metadata value. It stores: name: full path or backend path size: bytes, usually 0 for directories file_type: FileType::File, FileType::Directory, or FileType::Other created and modified: optional SystemTime values extra: backend-specific string metadata such as S3 ETags Convenience constructors are available: let file = FileInfo::file("/tmp/data.bin", 1024); let dir = FileInfo::directory("/tmp"); OpenMode::from_str_mode() accepts rb, wb, ab, xb, and the equivalent single-letter forms. OpenOptions::default() uses a 4 MiB block size, autocommit = true, no explicit cache strategy, and max_blocks = 32.

LocalFs uses std::fs and implements FileSystem. LocalFs::new() starts with auto_mkdir = false. LocalFs::with_auto_mkdir(true) creates missing parent directories during write, append, exclusive-create, and copy operations.

S3Fs wraps object_store::aws::AmazonS3 and runs its async calls through an embedded Tokio runtime to implement the synchronous FileSystem trait. S3Fs and the registry’s s3 protocol come from the s3 feature, which is on by default. With default-features = false the crate does not depend on object_store or Tokio and builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown: [dependencies] fsspec_rs = { version = "0.2", default-features = false } S3Config supports: bucket region endpoint_url access_key_id secret_access_key session_token anon virtual_hosted_style_request Plain HTTP is allowed automatically when endpoint_url starts with http://, which is useful for MinIO and LocalStack.

FilesystemRegistry maps URL protocols to FilesystemFactory implementations, the Rust counterpart of fsspec’s fsspec.specs entry points. Rust has no runtime plugin discovery, so a backend crate exports a factory and the application registers it. Any Fn(&str, &FsOptions) -> FsResult<SharedFileSystem> closure is a factory. url_to_fs(url, options) returns a SharedFileSystem and the path to pass to it. A URL without protocol:// is a local path. Options are a FsOptions (BTreeMap<String, String>). Chained URLs such as simplecache::s3://... are not supported. Filesystems are cached by protocol, options, and the factory’s instance_scope for the path, so equal calls share one instance. url_to_fs_uncached always builds a new one. Registering a protocol again replaces its factory and drops its cached instances. FilesystemRegistry::default() registers: Protocol Filesystem Options file, local LocalFs auto_mkdir memory MemoryFs, one per process none s3 S3Fs, one instance per bucket key, secret, token, endpoint_url, region, anon, virtual_hosted_style_request Unknown options are rejected. Boolean options accept true, false, 1, and 0. FilesystemRegistry::empty() starts with no protocols. DEFAULT_FIL

fsspec_rs_bridge exports PyFsspecFs, url_to_fs, and StorageOptions. It is an rlib using PyO3 and Python fsspec at runtime, with no #[pyclass] exports. url_to_fs(url, options) returns a filesystem adapter and start path. PyFsspecFs::from_protocol(protocol, options) constructs an adapter by protocol. The adapter’s trait protocol is python; source_protocol() reports the wrapped protocol. The bridge initializes and attaches to the Python interpreter internally. PyFsspecFs implements FileSystem and delegates ls, info, open, cat_file, pipe_file, cp_file, rm_file, mkdir, rmdir, get_file, and put_file to Python. Common Python exceptions map to FsError categories. StorageOptions values support nulls, booleans, signed and unsigned integers, floats, strings, lists, and nested maps. Nested maps keyed by protocol configure chained URLs. The Rust guide includes dependency and invocation examples.

The caching layer is used by buffered reads. CacheType::from_str() accepts: Value Strategy none NoCache: every fetch goes to the backend. readahead or read_ahead ReadAheadCache: one lookahead window. block or blockcache BlockCache: fixed-size blocks with LRU eviction. all or bytes AllBytesCache: whole-file cache on first read. Each cache wraps a Fetcher, a FnMut(u64, u64) -> FsResult<Vec<u8>> that retrieves the half-open byte range [start, end) from the backend.

All trait methods return FsResult<T> = Result<T, FsError>. FsError represents filesystem errors with these variants: NotFound PermissionDenied AlreadyExists NotADirectory IsADirectory IoError InvalidArgument NotSupported Other The PyO3 layer maps those variants to Python exceptions such as FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, FileExistsError, NotADirectoryError, IsADirectoryError, ValueError, NotImplementedError, and OSError.

fsspec-rs Use Rust-backed local and S3 filesystems through fsspec. Build Status codecov License PyPI fsspec-rs provides Python classes that inherit from fsspec.AbstractFileSystem and delegate core I/O to Rust. The native Rust crate provides shared filesystem traits, local and S3 backends, and read caches. A separate bridge crate adapts Python fsspec implementations for Rust callers. Documentation Start with Read and write a local file for a Python example. Use Rust-backed filesystems covers backend selection, S3 endpoints, and caching. Use the Rust crates covers native and Python-backed Rust access. Look up filesystem behavior, Rust traits and types, or the Python API. Why fsspec-rs uses explicit protocols and shared traits explains the design decisions.

Cargo license overrides The hatch-rs build hook uses license-overrides.json to supply license texts that cargo-bundle-licenses 4.2.0 cannot discover. The file contains r-efi 6.0.0, jni 0.22.4, jni-macros 0.22.4, jni-sys-macros 0.4.1, and rustls-platform-verifier-android 0.2.0, matched by package name, version, and license identifier. Other dependencies are collected from their source distributions at build time. These overrides require human review before shipping. They do not certify license compliance or change the crates’ declared license choices. Sources r-efi declares MIT OR Apache-2.0 OR LGPL-2.1-or-later.
